text: Life in Iceland after the initial colonization was not easy. Research on the skeletal remains from the Mosfell Valley has shown that people lived under harsh conditions, experienced malnutrition, and were afflicted by diseases and other physical ailments. Forensic archaeological research on the 20 skeletons from Hrísbrú have shown evidence of both tuberculosis and cancer from around the year 1000. The historian Magnús Guðmundsson, an expert on the team, says that a skull from a man in his thirties showed that the man died of an abscess in his brain, probably a very painful death. The research on these skeletons shows that the people had a life expectancy of about 40 to 45 years. The skeletons from Hrísbrú are also smaller than other skeletons uncovered in Iceland from the same period.
